p: Most people come to M&D's for the rides and head straight home again, which is a shame, because Strathclyde Country Park and the towns around it have plenty to fill another afternoon. The park wraps itself around Strathclyde Loch, a big man-made loch created in the 1970s, and its flat paths are perfect for a walk, a cycle or a scoot while the grown-ups enjoy a slower pace.

Tucked away in the park are the remains of a Roman bathhouse, linked to the fort at Bothwellhaugh. When the loch was created, the bathhouse was carefully moved to higher ground so it wouldn't be lost under the water, and it's a surprising little slice of history to stumble upon between theme-park rides. The loch is also used for watersports, so on a busy day you'll see rowers, paddlers and sailors out on the water.

A beer garden at a theme park is really about pacing the day. Pick your moment, ideally between the busiest ride rush and the late-afternoon slump, grab a table and let the younger ones go on a ride or two within sight while you recharge. Sun cream and a hat aren't just for beaches, as a sunny afternoon in a beer garden can catch you out, even in Scotland.

Hamilton is right next door, home to the Hamilton Mausoleum with its famously long echo, and Chatelherault Country Park with its woodland walks along the Avon Gorge. Motherwell town centre and Glasgow are both a short drive away if you want a bigger choice of restaurants for the evening, and the M74 makes getting in and out of the park straightforward.
